fixes.explanation: I get why you'd think so. Job did go quiet earlier (Job 40:4, 5), and a quiet man usually gets to sit down. But the LORD isn't done with him. He says, “Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.” (Job 40:7)

That's right. Job did go quiet earlier (Job 40:4, 5), but his silence doesn't end anything. The LORD says, “Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.” (Job 40:7) So Job isn't off the hook yet. He's being asked to answer.

Yes. The LORD says, “Then I will confess to you that your own right hand can save you.” (Job 40:14) Notice the "then." It comes after the LORD's whole list of challenges: an arm like God's, a voice that thunders, humbling the proud and trampling the wicked. (Job 40:9 to 13) The confession is only on the table if Job could pull all of that off.
Yes. “Though the river rages, Behemoth is unafraid; he remains secure, though the Jordan surges to his mouth.” (Job 40:23) Raging water doesn't rattle him. I'd be doing laps on my gold base.

Yes, baker, that's it. “One scale is so near to another that no air can pass between them.” (Job 41:16) That's armor with no gaps, and no gaps means nothing slips through. The next verse says, “They are joined to one another; they clasp and cannot be separated.” (Job 41:17) Tight and sealed together is the picture.
